notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1989:A.2.30.3 AR4: "Argument-2, if specified, must be a nonnumeric literal or alphanumeric data item." The 1989 text puts no rule on the content of argument-2 (§1989:A.2.30.3 AR1: "cs is the string of one or more characters specified by argument-2"). The class half conforms at 85: CheckArgumentClasses screens the Verified NUMVAL-C row and Violation refuses a numeric literal (the witness), a numeric item and an arithmetic expression with COBOL1627, and accepts an alphanumeric item and a group. The content half does not: BindNumvalCFamily applies §2023:15.68.3 AR2's bans ("Argument-2 shall not contain any of the digits 0 through 9", the characters * + - , . and CR or DB) to a literal argument-2 with no edition arm, and the runtime InvalidCurrency applies them to a data item, so at --std 85 a nonnumeric literal such as "Fr." or "C1" is refused and a data item holding one makes the function return 0. The same mechanism is recorded on 1989-AR-A.2.30.3-1. Probed also at 85: an alphabetic (PIC A) argument-2 is refused with COBOL1627, which fits the rule's words "alphanumeric data item".

next.reason: 1989: argument-2 'must be a nonnumeric literal or alphanumeric data item', no content rule. §2023:15.68.3 AR2: 'shall be of the same class as argument-1' (alphanumeric or national per §2023:15.68.3 AR1), shall contain a non-space character and shall not contain digits, '*', '+', '-', ',', '.', 'CR' or 'DB'. National is added and those currency strings, valid in 1989, are now refused. Differs both ways.
